questions.stem: During the day, plants both photosynthesise and respire. Which gas exchange would you observe overall from a well-lit plant?

options.text: Net uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide
Net uptake of carbon dioxide and release of oxygen, because photosynthesis rate exceeds respiration rate in bright light
No gas exchange at all
Equal uptake of both oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: During the day in bright light, the rate of photosynthesis exceeds the rate of respiration. Photosynthesis uses more CO2 than respiration produces, and produces more O2 than respiration uses. So the net effect is uptake of CO2 and release of O2. At night, only respiration occurs, so the plant takes in O2 and releases CO2.

questions.stem: The 'compensation point' is when the rate of photosynthesis exactly equals the rate of respiration. At this point, what is the net gas exchange of the plant?

options.text: The plant releases large amounts of oxygen
The plant releases large amounts of carbon dioxide
There is no net gas exchange -- all CO2 from respiration is used in photosynthesis, and all O2 from photosynthesis is used in respiration
The plant stops all metabolic activity

questions.explanation: At the compensation point, photosynthesis and respiration are occurring at exactly the same rate. The CO2 produced by respiration is used up by photosynthesis, and the O2 produced by photosynthesis is used up by respiration. There is no net exchange of gases with the environment. This typically occurs at low light intensities (e.g., dawn/dusk).

questions.stem: Stomata are mainly found on the lower surface of leaves. What is the advantage of this positioning?

options.text: The lower surface receives more light for photosynthesis
The lower surface is more shaded and cooler, reducing water loss through transpiration while still allowing gas exchange
The lower surface is closer to the soil where CO2 comes from
There is no advantage; it is random

questions.explanation: Having stomata on the lower surface means they are shaded from direct sunlight and sheltered from wind, reducing the rate of evaporation and therefore water loss. The upper surface, exposed to the sun, would lose water much faster if stomata were located there. This arrangement balances the need for gas exchange with water conservation.

questions.stem: The air spaces in the spongy mesophyll increase the internal surface area of the leaf. Why is a large internal surface area important for gas exchange?

options.text: It helps the leaf float on water
It provides a large moist surface from which water can evaporate, and across which CO2 can dissolve and diffuse into mesophyll cells for photosynthesis
It stores oxygen for use at night
It reduces the weight of the leaf

questions.explanation: CO2 must dissolve in the thin film of water on the surface of mesophyll cells before it can be used in photosynthesis. A large internal surface area (created by the air spaces between spongy mesophyll cells) provides more moist cell surfaces for this gas exchange to occur, increasing the overall rate of CO2 absorption and O2 release.

questions.stem: A student places a plant in a sealed container with hydrogencarbonate indicator (which changes from orange to yellow in high CO2 and purple in low CO2). After 24 hours in bright light, the indicator turns purple. What does this show?

options.text: The plant only respired
The plant removed more CO2 through photosynthesis than it added through respiration, reducing CO2 concentration
The indicator malfunctioned
The plant produced carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Purple indicates low CO2 concentration. In bright light, the rate of photosynthesis exceeds respiration, so the plant has consumed more CO2 than it has produced over 24 hours, lowering the CO2 concentration in the container. If the container were kept in darkness, the indicator would turn yellow (high CO2 from respiration only).
